memory_update.text: WEST appears to be the cleanest public small-cap mapping to private-label and foodservice coffee/beverage solutions, with direct restaurant and foodservice channel language in its 2025 10-K.
FARM is highly node-pure but should be treated as a speculative micro-cap exception until liquidity, leverage, customer retention, margin durability and DSD route economics are verified.
THS is less pure but relevant as a private-label coffee capacity owner after acquiring Farmer Bros.' Northlake facility and non-DSD business; verify materiality of coffee and foodservice exposure.

Need primary-source customer evidence for any claim that specific named restaurant chains use Farmer Bros., Westrock, or TreeHouse as coffee suppliers; current named-chain evidence is mostly third-party and should not survive later layers without contract, filing, or management confirmation.

FARM should be carried forward as the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for private-label coffee roasting, DSD beverage supply, and coffee-equipment service, but it is a micro-cap/speculative exception requiring liquidity, balance sheet, and customer verification.
THS should be tracked as a second-order private-label coffee capacity candidate because it acquired Farmer Brothers' Northlake facility and non-DSD business.
JVA may fit the obscure coffee-supplier screen, but current support is hypothesis-level only; do not advance without filings-based proof of foodservice/private-label/customer exposure.

Need a dedicated search for public coffee-equipment service networks, beverage syrup/concentrate vendors, and DSD operators; the supplied evidence mainly supports FARM and THS, with limited proof for broader equipment or ingredient pure-plays.

WEST is the best underfollowed public-company fit for the node: small-cap, direct exposure to coffee/tea/extract/private-label/RTD beverage solutions, and explicit foodservice/restaurant/hospitality/customer-channel language.

THS should be tracked as a hidden coffee/private-label asset rather than a restaurant pure-play; key diligence is whether the Farmer Brothers Northlake/direct-ship acquisition creates material coffee category growth or remains buried in a broad private-label portfolio.

JVA is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate: direct private-label and foodservice coffee relevance but below USD 300M, likely illiquid, and needs customer concentration, balance sheet, margin and commodity pass-through verification before surviving Layer 2.

FARM was historically one of the cleanest public pure-plays for DSD foodservice coffee, equipment service, and hidden chain/customer relationships, but evidence indicates it completed a take-private transaction with Royal Cup in May 2026; retain it as a private benchmark/customer map, not as a current US-listed candidate.

Need a follow-up search specifically for coffee-equipment service networks, beverage-dispensing service vendors, syrups/concentrates, office-coffee-service rollups, and restaurant beverage QA/testing suppliers; current evidence is stronger for roasters/co-manufacturers/distributors than for equipment-service chokepoints.

WEST should be retained as the highest-quality underfollowed candidate for the private-label coffee and beverage-solutions node because it has direct restaurant/foodservice, private-label, extract, RTD, and beverage-development exposure.

FARM is a highly direct but speculative micro-cap exposure to foodservice coffee, DSD distribution, and equipment service; later layers must stress-test balance sheet, liquidity, commodity sensitivity, and route economics.

THS is an adjacent private-label platform with acquired coffee-roasting capability; include as an underfollowed coffee-infrastructure mapping but verify how much of the acquired coffee business is restaurant or foodservice versus retail private label.

JVA is a speculative shadow candidate below the preferred market-cap threshold; it fits wholesale/private-label/foodservice coffee screening but requires proof of material restaurant or multi-unit foodservice exposure.

Need a follow-up pass on coffee-equipment service networks, beverage syrup/concentrate suppliers, cold-brew extract manufacturers, and DSD beverage distributors that may be public but not classified as coffee companies.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B universe expansion found a narrow US-listed set for restaurant and foodservice coffee/beverage supply. The most node-pure names are Westrock Coffee and Farmer Bros.; TreeHouse Foods is a larger private-label coffee capacity owner after buying Farmer Bros.' Northlake facility and non-DSD business; Starbucks is included only as a high-attention reference anchor for roasting, beverage menu demand, and foodservice coffee economics. This is research universe construction only, not a buy/sell recommendation. This pass expands the investable universe around obscure foodservice coffee and beverage suppliers rather than restaurant brands. The strongest underfollowed candidate is Farmer Brothers because the provided evidence directly ties it to private-label coffee, foodservice/hospitality customers, DSD, beverage ingredients, coffee-equipment service, and a pricing engine. TreeHouse Foods enters as a second-order private-label consolidator because it acquired Farmer Brothers' Northlake facility and non-DSD business. Coffee Holding enters only as a speculative micro-cap hypothesis because it plausibly fits wholesale/private-label coffee exposure but lacks evidence in the supplied context. Starbucks is included only as a reference/customer-context anchor, not as the intended alpha target. Expanded the universe for the foodservice coffee and beverage-supply node with a two-lane funnel.
